q-341490.name: Question 1
q-341490.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cosecant function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsch}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}\{arcsch[\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)]\} \\  & =-\frac{1}{|\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)|\sqrt{1+[\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)]^{2}}}\cdot [\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)]^{′} \\  & =-\frac{1}{|\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)|\sqrt{1+[\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)]^{2}}}\cdot \frac{1}{x} \\  & =-\frac{1}{x|\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)|}\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+[\operatorname{ln}⁡(x)]^{2}}}\end{aligned}
$$

q-95514.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cosecant function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsch}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{1+{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-4\operatorname{arcsch}⁡{e}^{x}) \\  & =-4\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcsch}⁡{e}^{x}) \\  & =-4\cdot (-\frac{1}{|{e}^{x}|\sqrt{1+{({e}^{x})}^{2}}})\cdot ({e}^{x})^{′} \\  & =4\cdot \frac{1}{{e}^{x}\cdot \sqrt{1+{e}^{2x}}}\cdot {e}^{x} \\  & =\frac{4}{\sqrt{1+{e}^{2x}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-341504.name: Question 3
q-341504.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic secant function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsech}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{x\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}-1)+\operatorname{arsech}⁡({x}^{2}-1)] \\  & =\frac{{({x}^{2}-1)}^{′}}{{x}^{2}-1}-\frac{1}{({x}^{2}-1)\sqrt{1-{({x}^{2}-1)}^{2}}}\cdot {({x}^{2}-1)}^{′} \\  & =\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}-1}-\frac{1}{({x}^{2}-1)\sqrt{1-({x}^{4}-2{x}^{2}+1)}}\cdot 2x \\  & =\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}-1}-\frac{2x}{({x}^{2}-1)\sqrt{2{x}^{2}-{x}^{4}}} \\  & =\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}-1}[1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}(2-{x}^{2})}}].\end{aligned}
$$

q-95341.name: Question 6
q-95341.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic cotangent function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arcoth}⁡({x}^{2}+1)) \\  & =\frac{1}{1-({x}^{2}+1)^{2}}\cdot ({x}^{2}+1)^{′} \\  & =\frac{1}{1-({x}^{2}+1)^{2}}\cdot 2x \\  & =\frac{2x}{1-({x}^{2}+1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2x}{1-({x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}+1)} \\  & =-\frac{2x}{{x}^{4}+2{x}^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{2x}{{x}^{2}({x}^{2}+2)} \\  & =-\frac{2}{x({x}^{2}+2)}.\end{aligned}

q-95345.name: Question 11
q-95345.worked_solution:
In this case, the expression for $f(x)$ is a quotient $\frac{u(x)}{v(x)}$ with $u(x)=\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x$ and $v(x)={x}^{2}.$ 

Therefore, we apply the quotient rule as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x)^{′}\cdot {x}^{2}-\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x\cdot ({x}^{2})^{′}}{({x}^{2})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x)^{′}\cdot {x}^{2}}{{x}^{4}}-\frac{\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x\cdot ({x}^{2})^{′}}{{x}^{4}} \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x)^{′}}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x\cdot (2x)}{{x}^{4}} \\  & =\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\cdot (\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x)^{′}-\frac{2\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x}{{x}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\cdot \frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}-\frac{2\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x}{{x}^{3}} \\  & ={{\frac{1}{{x}^{2}(1-{x}^{2})}}_{⏟}}_{g(x)}-\frac{2\operatorname{arcoth}⁡x}{{x}^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $g(x)=\frac{1}{{x}^{2}(1-{x}^{2})}.$
